summary.headline: Sportking India Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 19.8% from 10.4% a year ago, with management guiding H2 margins close to H1 levels.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, attributing the margin expansion to better yarn demand over the last two to three quarters, cost-efficiency programmes, and stable cotton prices over the past year. Exports were about 52% of revenue in Q2. The 150,000-spindle Greenfield project in Odisha is nearly built, machinery is arriving and erection is underway, and commercial production is guided within 30 to 40 days. Management said yarn spreads are similar to the past six months and guided margins to stay close to H1 levels, with a 15% EBITDA floor and upside not guaranteed.

financial_highlights.value: about INR17 crore per quarter from next quarter
financial_highlights.change: vs INR24 crore in Q1 and INR14 crore in Q2 per management
vs INR396.2 crore at Mar-26; about 58 days in both periods per management

financial_highlights.metric: Combined fabric and garment entities EBITDA
financial_highlights.change: about 20% EBITDA contribution per management; potential about INR100 crore, down about INR20 crore due to stoppages

segments.name: Spinning (cotton and blended yarn)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation at 99% in Q2 per management; exports about 52% of revenue. Demand from China and Bangladesh described as robust, with Bangladesh at about 45,000-50,000 tons and China buying about 60,000 tons.

segments.name: Fabric and garment entities (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Not yet merged; management expects merger within a couple of months. Combined H1 EBITDA ballparked at about INR80 crore, with output below potential due to restructuring stoppages.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 margins expected to stay close to H1 levels on the existing capacity; management declined to give a specific figure (19%, 18% or 21%).
Spreads guided at INR130-145/kg for the next three to four months; management said deviation of plus or minus 2% is possible.
Odisha 150,000-spindle project: commercial production in 30-40 days; FY27 contribution INR150-200 crore; FY28 revenue INR1,200-1,300 crore.
Odisha margins guided at least 4-5% (possibly 6%) above current company margins once operational; management said EBITDA positive from day one.
Peak long-term debt by March 2027 about INR700-750 crore; working capital below INR200 crore.
FY28: management reiterated at least 15% EBITDA margin, with upside possible but not guaranteed.
capex_capacity: Odisha Greenfield: 150,000 spindles, INR1,000 crore investment; building construction almost complete; full machinery package ordered and arriving in stages.
Commissioning of initial machinery expected in coming months; management said the whole project should finish by March 2027.
Solar power project commissioned; expected to cut annual power costs by about 15%.

Odisha incentives: 30% capital subsidy (about INR200-220 crore over 5 years), power at INR4/unit for 10 years, employment subsidy of INR7,000-8,000 per worker per month for 5 years, plus land-price rebate after 1,000 jobs.

Phase 2: land for another 300,000 spindles in Odisha; brownfield phase expected to take 2-3 months less than the Greenfield timeline; management said a second-phase trigger is expected in roughly 6-8 months, subject to debt levels.
Garment expansion plans to be announced possibly in H2 of next year.
demand_pricing: Management said yarn demand has risen for two to three quarters; visibility runs to about 10 March 2027, with demand the same or better.
Sales are typically on 80-90 day windows and about 120-day LC-backed credit terms.

Cotton prices fell from about INR70,000/candy to about INR65,500/candy; imported cotton landed at about INR67,000/candy per management. Blended cotton cost about INR150-160/kg (up from INR150 in Q1 per management).

Management expects Indian cotton prices to ease after Diwali, while the Indian yarn peak season after Diwali supports demand. Import duty waiver expected to be extended to December 2026 (per management, not yet notified).
Competition: management said new spindle announcements have been limited; consolidation and compliance costs are restricting smaller players.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin rise to 19.8% from 10.4%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better cotton and blended yarn demand over two to three quarters, operational efficiency gains from cost work over two to three years, and stable cotton prices over the past year; it expects similar conditions in the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Odisha project on track for Q3 FY27 commencement?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction is nearly complete and erection is underway; commercial production is expected in 30-40 days, with completion targeted by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 contribution and FY28 revenue from Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided INR150-200 crore in FY27 and INR1,200-1,300 crore in FY28; margins at Odisha expected to be 4-6% above current company margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are current spreads and how are inventory and cotton costs managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads are similar to the past six months; Q2 about INR141/kg versus INR133/kg in Q1; expected INR130-145/kg for three to four months. The company holds some cotton stock, sources from about 10 countries, and keeps about 3 months of order book cover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise to INR473.5 crore from INR396.2 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to higher billing and sales, LC-backed credit terms of about 120 days, and said receivable days are unchanged at about 58 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 margins and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated at least 15% EBITDA margin for FY28 with upside not guaranteed; peak long-term debt about INR700-750 crore by March 2027 and working capital below INR200 crore.

risks_watch: Cotton prices may rise if the monsoon and crop outlook weaken; management expects a moderate decline after Diwali but said volatility is high.
Import duty waiver on cotton expires 31 October 2026; extension to December not yet notified per management.
Odisha commissioning timing and ramp-up pace, given the 'record time' build.
Receivables and LC-backed credit terms (about 120 days) and rising working capital.
Merger of the fabric and garment entities requires preferential allotment of non-convertible shares and cash of INR25-30 crore; regulatory completion pending.
Depreciation run-rate guidance changed after a method change (about INR7-8 crore impact).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the Odisha timeline, but guarded on specific numbers: management declined to give exact margins, cotton cost per kg and exact FY28 guidance, and some answers were loosely specified.
key_quotes: So the key factors are of course vis-à-vis last year is the improved demand.
we expect the margins to stay almost where we were in the first half.
So I think right now the demand of yarn is pretty solid and we think any incremental increase in cotton is going to increase the yarn prices as well.
But I think we can assure 15%, but anything more than that is likely, but not guaranteed.

adds.what: 150,000-spindle Greenfield yarn plant in Odisha (INR1,000 crore)
Phase 2: land for 300,000 spindles in Odisha (brownfield)

growth.why: Management guides Odisha 150,000-spindle plant to add INR150-200 crore FY27 revenue and INR1,200-1,300 crore in FY28, with commercial production in 30-40 days and existing plants at 99% utilisation; backing is partly specific (capex, incentives, timeline) but FY28 revenue and margin guidance is not tied to firm orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 19.8% in Q2 from 10.4% a year ago, and management guides H2 close to H1 levels with a 15% floor; spreads rose to INR141/kg from INR133/kg, though upside is not guaranteed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha 150,000-spindle Greenfield (INR1,000 crore) is nearly built with erection under way and commercial production guided in 30-40 days, with completion targeted by March 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Existing spinning capacity runs at 99% utilisation, and Odisha adds INR150-200 crore FY27 revenue once live, with visibility to about 10 March 2027 showing demand the same or better.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Phase 2 land for 300,000 spindles in Odisha is already acquired and management expects a second-phase trigger in roughly 6-8 months, subject to debt levels; utilisation at 99% with no spare capacity supports this.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says FY28 EBITDA margin is at least 15% with upside 'likely but not guaranteed', and Q2 margin of 19.8% is well above that floor.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cotton may rise if monsoon weakens and the import duty waiver expires 31 October 2026 without notified extension; the merged fabric/garment entities are running about INR20 crore below potential due to stoppages.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Garment expansion plans are to be announced possibly in H2 of next year, with no product or launch detail given.

rows.label: Odisha plant ramp to INR1,200-1,300 crore FY28 revenue
rows.why: Management guides Odisha FY28 revenue at INR1,200-1,300 crore and margins 4-6% above company margins, though this is not tied to firm orders and commissioning timing is subject to ramp-up pace.

rows.label: Peak long-term debt INR700-750 crore by March 2027
rows.why: Management guides peak long-term debt at about INR700-750 crore with working capital below INR200 crore, while the Odisha capex and Phase 2 land are funded alongside.

rows.label: Receivables rising with LC-backed 120-day terms
rows.why: Trade receivables rose to INR473.5 crore from INR396.2 crore (about 58 days unchanged), so working capital pressure may persist as billing grows.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 19.8% margin, and the Odisha timeline, but declined exact H2 margin, cotton cost and FY28 figures; analysts pressed on sustainability of margins, receivables and the Odisha ramp.
